title: Höpken and Carlson, Pera, to the King of Sweden, despatch No. 2 of 15/26 January 1740: transcribed from the contemporary Swedish decipherment written over a second numerical code, code list rebuilt, digits checked against a bare second copy

documents.shelfmark: Stockholm, Riksarkivet, Diplomatica Turcica, SE/RA/2119/2119.1/I/9/21 (image series R0003582), images 321-331 (second copy 332-342)
documents.route: Carl Fredrik Höpken and Edvard Carlson, Constantinople -> the King of Sweden

plaintext.source: Contemporary decipherment in Swedish written over the struck-through groups by the chancery decipherer.

transcription.source: Riksarkivet IIIF images, full size (lbiiif.riksarkivet.se, R0003582)
transcription.notes: Word-level pairs by five AI agents with the gloss in view; a bare second copy (332, 334-342) transcribed digits-only and blind by three agents, 2,987 of 3,082 groups identical; 116 digits taken from the bare copy; doubtful lines rechecked twice.

system.summary: Numerical code of four-digit groups seen between 1006 and 1915: a syllabary (a/å/ä, o/ö, i/j, u/v not distinguished) with word codes for names and terms. Different from the code of images 255-261 (hopken1739).
system.notes: Seed values read by eye only; no key built.

prior_solution.where: The contemporary Swedish decipherment written over the groups on images 322-327. No edition or modern decipherment found (web searches, 10 Nov 2026).

conditions.human_role: Daniel Bourdeau set the task; AI language-model agents transcribed. No human palaeographer checked the text.

solution.what: Images 322-327 of R0003582 fetched from the Riksarkivet IIIF service at full size.
Pass 1 by two AI agents with the Swedish gloss in view: 123 runs, 2118 groups (pairs_322_324.tsv, pairs_325_327.tsv); 23 runs K. Gloss column rough and loosely aligned.
Groups above 1749 (to about 1999) and value clashes with the French-glossed code of 255-261 show a second code; split from hopken1739.
Hard-EM segmentation on the 23 K runs with 9 seeds: alignments are not usable (gloss extents too loose). Word-level re-pairing started.
Word-level pairs re-read from full-size crops by three agents (wordpairs_*.tsv): gloss word, groups under it, segmentation; 2,119 groups.
Key from the K lines of 322-325 frozen (key_frozen_322_325.tsv): 147 confirmed, 15 mixed, 67 single.

Held-out test on 326-327: 457 of 598 groups give exactly the piece of the pairing (522 in key); shuffled-key control mean 3.5, max 33 of 500. Not strictly blind: the 326-327 agent had seeds.tsv and could have seen the 324-325 pairs. Rerun after the recheck of doubtful lines (more K lines on 326-327): 525 of 687.

Recheck of the 94 doubtful lines with the full key: 63 settled, 31 remain. Final key 190 confirmed / 23 mixed / 87 single. 2,027 of 2,119 groups (95.7%) in confident words. Swedish reading and English translation written.
Images 319-321 and 328-342 fetched: the despatch is No. 2 of 15/26 Jan 1740, images 321-331; images 332-342 are a second copy in the same encipherment (332-333 glossed, 334-342 bare).
Word-level pairs for 321 and 328-331 by two agents with key.tsv in view (1,331 groups).

Bare second copy transcribed digits-only by three agents told to open no other file: 3,082 groups, 2,987 identical in sequence to the glossed copy. 116 digits taken from the bare copy at one-for-one differences (scripts/apply_bare.py).

Second recheck of the 63 doubtful lines against both copies: 51 settled, 11 remain. Final key 235 confirmed / 15 mixed / 78 single; 3,411 of 3,450 groups (98.9%) in confident words. Reading and translation extended to the whole despatch.

outcome.method_basis: The text is the 18th-century Swedish decipherment written over the groups, transcribed word by word; the code list rebuilt from it was frozen on four pages and tested on two more, and the digits were checked against a blind transcription of a bare second copy.
outcome.fraction_read_source: 3,411 of 3,450 groups on images 321-331 lie in words whose digits and reading are both confident (scripts/make_texts.py).

credits.note: the chancery decipherer's Swedish written over the groups on images 322-327

gaps.detail: both copies agree on the digits; the word reads from the gloss

gaps.item: 3 words where the split between groups is unknown (1640, 1689, 1771)
gloss over 1313 on 323 l08 unread (a name)
a few clear words doubtful in the hand

texts.summary: Höpken and Carlson report to the King how the Porte's dragoman brought the signed defensive alliance treaty and asked to delay its exchange and keep it secret, how they argued for a prompt exchange, and how the exemplars were exchanged on 14/25 January 1740 after a present to Ragib Efendi. They credit the King's firmness over the Russian frontier, note the French ambassador's late help, and ask for a provisional instruction and full powers.

reading_review.by: Claude (AI model), reading the Swedish text as sentences while translating it
reading_review.note: Coherent throughout; holes at 11 doubtful words and a few clear words.
